cohort: Sixty preeclamptic women undergoing caesarean section were randomly divided into a magnesium sulfate group and a control group.
finding: Intravenous magnesium sulfate hastened the onset of sensory block, prolonged the duration of sensory block, motor block, and spinal anesthesia, and alleviated postoperative pain in preeclamptic women without additional side effects, but did not hasten the onset of motor block.
